title: Derived adic completeness
statement:
Let $E/\Ql$ be finite, with uniformizer $\pi_E$, and let
$\mathcal O_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ and $(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ be
the integral and finite coefficient sheaves of
[sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. A complex
$K\in D(X_{\Proet},\mathcal O_E)$ is *derived complete* if its canonical map

$$
K\longrightarrow R\varprojlim_n\bigl(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism. For
$K_n=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$, the canonical
transitions satisfy the derived reduction identities
$K_{n+1}\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^{n+1})_X}(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X\simeq K_n$;
a compatible tower with these identities is called *normalized*.

Normalization is a property of the complexes $K_n$; their cohomology sheaves
$H^q(K_n)$ need not form a normalized tower under the ordinary tensor product.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_{E,X}$ and $B_n=(\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n)_X$, $n\ge1$. The coefficient constructions give $R\to B_{n+1}\to B_n$. Use the unbounded Layer B category $D(\Mod_R)$ and its relative derived tensor.

source.place: coefficient sheaves and ambient derived category

proof.text: With the sheafified closed tensor of [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure] and [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], use [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] on a small site in the coefficient universe. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. $P$ is also K-flat in the sense of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]: for a quasi-isomorphism $u$, $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R\operatorname{Cone}u)\cong\operatorname{Cone}(P\otimes_Ru)$ is acyclic, and symmetrically. So the statement's derived extension [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars] and that of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] are both computed by $P\otimes_RB_n$ with unit $p\mapsto p\otimes1$; as left adjoints of the same exact restriction they agree with their units and adjoint transitions. Apply [lem-pe-kflat-scalar-tower-realization] to $R\to B_n$: it identifies the actual derived reductions, transitions and scalar units with $P_n=P\otimes_R B_n$, $t_n=1\otimes(B_{n+1}\to B_n)$ and $c_n(p)=p\otimes1$. Both composites $t_nc_{n+1}$ and $c_n$ send $p$ to $p\otimes1$, so the augmentation is strict.

source.place: Tags 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution, and 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; the new scalar-tower realization lemma retains the actual units and transitions

proof.text: Countable products are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Hence [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence](2) computes their derived product by $V=\prod_nP_n$. Define $s$ by $\mathrm{pr}_ns=t_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$. The strict-augmentation clause of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] identifies $(c,0):P\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ with the canonical derived-limit map. Its invertibility is independent of $P$ by [lem-pe-kflat-roos-representative-invariance]. Requiring this map to be invertible defines completeness.

source.place: Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit, and lemma-products; the specified augmentation is supplied by the cited strict comparison

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] to $R\to B_{n+1}\to B_n$. Its natural isomorphism is the displayed reduction identity and respects the scalar units. The actual transition has formula $p\otimes b\mapsto p\otimes\bar b$; its adjoint is $(p\otimes b)\otimes a\mapsto p\otimes\bar b a$, precisely that isomorphism. This proves normalization for the specified transitions.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition, specialized to coefficient changes

proof.text: For the warning take $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, and $K=[R\xrightarrow{\ell}R]$ in degrees $-1,0$. By [lem-pe-two-term-reduction-cohomology] its ordinary cohomology reduction comparison in degree $-1$ is zero between nonzero copies of $k_X$. It cannot be invertible: an inverse would imply $1_{k_X}=0$. Its complex reduction tower is normalized by step 4, giving the required distinction.

source.place: Final paragraph; the explicit cohomology and transition calculation is delegated to the new two-term reduction lemma
